bibl.author: Theodosius, the patriarch — ܦܛܪܝܪܟܐ ܬܐܘܕܘܣܝܘܣ

noteGrp.note: Syriac commentaries attributed to Theodosios of Antioch. Extant extracts include a letter to Eleazar Bishop of Cyros, a story of Hierotheos, prolegomena and commentaries on several chapters of the Book of Hierotheos. Through definitions, structured introductions, and close exegesis, the commentary combines Syriac biblical interpretation with Greek philosophical and Pseudo-Dionysian methods.

note.quote: ܐܠܐ ܘܡܛܠ ܕܡܠܬܢ ܥܘܬܕܗ ܕܗܢܐ ܟܬܒܐ ܕܩܕܝܫܐ ܐܝܪܬܐܘܣ ܡܚܘܐ: ܗܘ ܕܡܠܠ ܪܡܙܢܐܝܬ ܥܠ ܪܐܙܐ ܐܠܗܝܐ.
but, since the (following) Introduction to this Book of the holy Hierotheos, who speaks symbolically of Divine Mysteries, (sufficiently) sets forth our theme,
ܟܝܢܐ ܕܟܠܡܕܡ ܠܘܬ ܐܠܗܐ ܗܦܟ.ܢܛܘܪܘܬܐ ܕܪܐܙܐ ܐܝܩܪܐ ܕܐܠܐ.ܕܝܢܐ ܕܐܝܠܝܢ ܕܠܐ ܡܠܬܐ. ܡܢ ܟܝܢܗܘܢ ܡܬܝܕܥܝܢ: ܗܢܘ ܟܠ ܥܘܬܕܐ ܘܡܠܬܐ ܡܣܝܟܬܐ ܕܡܘܕܥܐ ܚܝܠܗ ܕܟܬܒܐ ܗܢܐ.

The Nature of Everything returns unto God. The Preservation of the Mysteries (is) the honour of God. The Judgement of Irrational Things..... (?) by their nature. This is the whole Introduction and the Concise Statement which makes known the sense of this Book.
